full_judgment:
Md Gholam Rabbani J : On 24-2-98 we passed order in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1998 that this matter should be heard along With Criminal' Appeal No. 106 of 1996. By this judgment we will dispose of both the appeal and the Rule. 

 3. Thereafter police arrested those two persons and ultimately submitted charge-sheet against them under section 5 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983. Consequently, the aforesaid accused persons were placed on trial before the Special Tribunal No. 2 and 1st Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Chittagong, in Special Tribunal Case No. 123 of 1995. 

 6. It appears that both the learned Advocates did not file bail bond and consequently the two girls could not come out from the jail custody. They however, obtained Rule from the High Court Division under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Misc. Case No. 19 of 1998 challenging their detention in the judicial custody. 

 9. In the case of HM Ershad vs. State reported in 45 DLR 433 it was held that consideration of the statements made under section 161 CrPC while framing charge or otherwise is the necessary part of the Court's duty. Trial Court has the wide power under the law regarding framing of charge. This can not be interfered with lightly either by the revisional court or the appellate Court. Usually police submits charge-sheet on the basis of the statements of the witnesses recorded under section 161 CrPC. If there is other statements of a witness like the statements recorded under section 164 CrPC that witness may be cross-examined as to his previous statements in terms of section 145 of the Evidence Act for the purpose of contradicting the witness, but that can be only after drawing attention of the witness to his pervious statements. We, therefore, hold that to frame a charge or to consider an application of the accused person that the charge brought against him is groundless trial Court is not obliged to consider the statements of any witness recorded under section 164 CrPC. We, therefore, find no illegality in the order dated 4-9-95 under appeal. 

 11. In the result Criminal Appeal No. 106 of 1996 is dismissed. Order of staying the further proceedings of the Special Tribunal Case No. 123 of 1995 of the 1st Court of the Additional Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal No.2, Chittagong, passed at the time of admitting the appeal is hereby vacated. 

 12. Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1998 is disposed of With' the direction that the learned Special Tribunal Judge should take evidence of Rina Begum and Fatema Begum within two months from the date of receipt .of the LC records and then shall discharge the two girls from the judicial custody after a reasonable time.
